metadata.technology_specification: Benchtop Flow Cytometer with Laser-Based Optical Detection
metadata.technology_reasoning: Benchtop flow cytometers with laser-based optical detection are the industry-standard form used broadly in research and clinical laboratories due to their versatility, reliability, and widespread adoption; laser optics enable multiparametric analysis with high sensitivity, dominating over older fluorescence or imaging cytometry forms.

components.reasoning: Fundamental for transporting cells in a fluid stream for interrogation; a distinct assembly including pumps, tubing, and sheath fluid reservoirs, universally present in all flow cytometers.
Provides the laser light sources for excitation of fluorochromes, a critical optical subassembly procured separately or modular in many instruments, essential for fluorescence-based detection.

components.component: Optical Detection System (Photomultiplier Tubes or Photodiodes)
components.reasoning: Core for collecting and converting fluorescence and scattered light signals; typically separate optical sensor modules with dedicated electronics, universally part of flow cytometers.

components.component: Electronic Signal Processing and Data Acquisition Board
components.reasoning: Processes and digitizes detector signals for analysis; a major separate PCB assembly present in essentially all devices.
Enables loading of samples into the fluidics stream; a distinct mechanical/electromechanical subassembly commonly replaced or calibrated separately.
Includes touchscreens or display panels and user input hardware, a discrete subassembly standard for operational control across modern systems.

components.component: Waste and Sheath Fluid Management Assembly
components.reasoning: Manages fluid disposal and sheath fluid recycling, a subsystem common in most designs but sometimes integrated or simplified in smaller instruments.
Provides mechanical housing and protection for all internal components, a standard separate assembly across instrument manufacturers.
